\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{पीहर} (pīhar)}{पीहर (pīhar)}]{\mw{पीहर} (pīhar) — a woman's parents' home}

\label{lesson:MW-C246-pihar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a surprise, then the Marwadi for congratulations.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{पीहर}}
\textbf{\mw{पीहर}} — \emph{pīhar} — \textquotedblleft{}a woman's parents' home\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{मां} \mw{काल} \mw{पीहर} \mw{गई।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mā̃ kāl pīhar gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mother went to her parents' home yesterday.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{पीहर}} (\emph{pīhar}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*pitṛghara}, \textquotedblleft{}father's house\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{pīhar} under it (CDIAL 8180).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pīhar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pīhar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mā̃ kāl pīhar gaī.} — Mother went to her parents' home yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a surprise, then the Marwadi for congratulations, then say \emph{pīhar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{पीहर} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A woman's parents' home\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सासरो} (sāsro)}{सासरो (sāsro)}]{\mw{सासरो} (sāsro) — a woman's in-laws' home}

\label{lesson:MW-C246-sasro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for congratulations, then the Marwadi for a woman's parents' home.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सासरो}}
\textbf{\mw{सासरो}} — \emph{sāsro} — \textquotedblleft{}a woman's in-laws' home\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{नूतो} (nūto)}{नूतो (nūto)}]{\mw{नूतो} (nūto) — an invitation (to a wedding or a feast)}

\label{lesson:MW-C246-nuto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a woman's parents' home, then the Marwadi for a woman's in-laws' home.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{नूतो}}
\textbf{\mw{नूतो}} — \emph{nūto} — \textquotedblleft{}an invitation (to a wedding or a feast)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{काल} \mw{गांव} \mw{सूं} \mw{नूतो} \mw{आयो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāl gā̃v sū̃ nūto āyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
An invitation came from the village yesterday.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{नूतो}} (\emph{nūto}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*nimantra}, \textquotedblleft{}invitation\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{nautā}, \textquotedblleft{}an invitation to a wedding\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7233).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{बीतणो} (bītṇo)}{बीतणो (bītṇo)}]{\mw{बीतणो} (bītṇo) — to pass (of time); to go by}

\label{lesson:MW-C246-bitno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a woman's in-laws' home, then the Marwadi for an invitation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{बीतणो}}
\textbf{\mw{बीतणो}} — \emph{bītṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to pass (of time); to go by\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{सियाळो} \mw{बीत्यो।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{siyāḷo bītyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cold season went by.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \mw{वो} \mw{महीनो} \mw{बीत्यो}, \emph{vo mahīno bītyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{बीतणो}} (\emph{bītṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{vṛtta}, \textquotedblleft{}turned\textquotedblright{}, and of time \textquotedblleft{}passed\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{bītnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12069).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bītṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siyāḷo bītyo.} — The cold season went by.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a woman's in-laws' home, then the Marwadi for an invitation, then say \emph{bītṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मरणो} (marṇo)}{मरणो (marṇo)}]{\mw{मरणो} (marṇo) — to die}

\label{lesson:MW-C246-marno-die}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for an invitation, then the Marwadi for to pass (of time).

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मरणो}}
\textbf{\mw{मरणो}} — \emph{marṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to die\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
